Listening safety. Audio can be uncomfortable or harmful at excessive output levels. Start low, especially with headphones. Perceived loudness is not a reliable measure of acoustic output. Digital signal generation does not guarantee that your hardware reproduces the requested frequency.

Limits

The limit is scheduled on the audio clock, so it holds even if the page stalls. A lower limit also ends the note that is sounding at its start plus the new limit. It also caps the Finite tone. Other programmed patterns stop at their own end (max 30 s), and a looped Pattern Sequencer sequence sounds for at most 30 s; a continuous sweep repeat or an endless sequencer loop needs “Allow continuous playback”.

    About · OSCILLA

    About OSCILLA

    See sound. Shape frequency.

    A zero-install, scientifically honest acoustic laboratory in your browser: generate, measure and reproduce sound experiments, and know how far each result can be trusted.

    Measure the response of your speaker, room and microphone chain, compare two setups with every difference named, save an experiment and repeat it, and patch a signal graph in the Studio.

    A Workspaces

    Every workspace of the navigation, in its order, and what it is for.

    • Playground The instrument on one screen: generator, waveform, spectrum, spectrogram, microphone analyzer, pattern sequencer and the labs.
    • Measure A guided measurement of the speaker, room and microphone chain: frequency response, impulse response and RTA, each run rated for quality.
    • Experiments Saved measurements as experiments: their definitions, a comparison against a baseline, and the findings that cite them.
    • Analyzer The microphone's live spectrum and spectrogram: a live view, not a calibrated measurement.
    • Filter Lab A biquad filter and the response the browser computes for it, set by type, cutoff and Q.
    • Compare The microphone analyzer beside the bioacoustics hearing ranges and the phase and stereo views.
    • Synthesis Additive harmonics, the ADSR envelope and the dual oscillator, with the compact Studio.
    • Sequencer Block sequences of tones, sweeps, pulses and modulation, beside the compact Studio.
    • Presets Built-in and saved instrument settings, and the history of what was played.
    • Learn Concept cards from frequency to speaker limitations, most with a demo to play.
    • Studio A signal graph you patch, with a timeline, transport and automation, run on Web Audio.
    • Synth A semi-modular mono voice on the Studio model with a patch bay and docked keys, and an Engines tab of additive, FM, AM and ring, wavetable, hard-sync and percussion voices.
    • About This page: what OSCILLA is, how it got here and what comes next.

    B What comes next

    The open milestones of OSCILLA's plan as of this release and how many of each one's required issues are done: now under way, next ready to start, later waiting on work above.

    C Origin

    OSCILLA began with an anti-bark ad promising “ultrasound through any phone's speaker” that only dogs would hear. A phone tone around 15–16 kHz is audible to many people, and it is not ultrasound. Its author's reply was “this can be knocked together in one HTML5”, and that night it grew into a lab.

    What it grew into asks a broader question: how much of an acoustic laboratory could live entirely inside a web browser?

    The first version was deliberately direct:

    1. Generate
    2. Hear
    3. See
    4. Inspect

    From there it grew into a denser instrument for frequency, phase, modulation, filtering, sequencing and microphone comparison, without hiding the signal path.

    D Engineering

    The speed was unusual. The constraints were deliberately not.

    • Deterministic The same source builds the same bytes; the committed file is the deployed file.
    • Protected V1 engine schedules are frozen and replayed; a browser gate runs Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
    • Verified The interface is compared against a visual reference.
    • Recorded Architecture decisions are written down with their reasons.
    • Honest Approximation is never presented as measurement; relative is not calibrated.
    • Private No server, no account, no analytics. A measurement's recording is discarded after its analysis; a saved run keeps derived results, whose impulse response can still carry room sound.

    Engineering system

    Majordomus

    A repository-native engineering control plane for human and AI contributors.

    OSCILLA explores sound and frequency. Its development explores a narrower question: can implementation speed rise without architecture, verification and product identity dissolving around it?

    Much of the implementation was AI-assisted. That is how OSCILLA is built, not why it exists.

    1. Human judgment defined the product and the architecture.
    2. AI accelerated implementation.
    3. Majordomus kept the rules, plan and decisions in the repository and checked them.
    4. The repository remained the source of truth.

    Instead of depending on an AI conversation to remember how OSCILLA should work, the repository carries its own machine-readable engineering context: every contributor, person or model, starts from the same rules and plan. Where it is checked: on each commit and in CI, Majordomus validates that context; before a push, a task's scope; and every pull request runs the test suites and a test that each path the claims, rules and guides name exists and each claim's test runs in CI. Review covers what no check can.

    Save preset

    Stored in this browser (localStorage, preset schema v1) with the Filter, Envelope, Additive and Phase & Stereo settings. The sequence is not included (it travels in the config file), and the continuous-playback permission is never stored.

    Headphones required

    Binaural beats need one tone per ear: put on headphones and keep the level low before you continue. Speakers mix both channels and the effect disappears.

    Config link

    The clipboard is not available here. Copy the link manually.

    Keyboard shortcuts

    In Playground

    Space (hold)
    Hold to play: sounds while held, stops on release (a programmed pattern: trigger once)

    Everywhere

    Space has one owner in each workspace. Where a workspace plays, loads or analyses the instrument's signal, holding Space plays it, whether or not a Play control is on screen. In Studio, Space starts or stops the Studio transport. Elsewhere it starts nothing. A focused text field, button, link, slider or open dialog keeps Space. Start at a low level: OSCILLA caps the logical gain at 0.25 and, unless continuous playback is allowed in Device & Limits, stops every tone after the hard limit and a looped Pattern Sequencer sequence at 30 s. A note held on the keyboard or a MIDI key sounds while it is held, under the same gain cap, and stops on release, Esc, or when the page loses the focus.

    Microphone

    The microphone starts only when you press “Use microphone”. Echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain are requested off, so the analyser sees the raw input. Audio never leaves this page.

    Detected frequencies come from the FFT peak (parabolic interpolation; autocorrelation below 1 kHz) and are never shown finer than the bin resolution. Use the Compare tab for freeze, averaging and peak hold.

    Not a calibrated measurement. From file:// some browsers refuse the microphone; the panel then says so.

    Settings

    Hard limit (Device & Limits): scheduled on the audio clock, so it holds even if the page stalls. It also caps the Finite tone. Other programmed patterns stop at their own end (max 30 s); a continuous sweep repeat needs “Allow continuous playback”. A note held on the keyboard or a MIDI key is exempt while it is held and stops on release, Esc, or when the page loses the focus. Attack applies from the next note. Release, edited while a note is held, is the fade when you let go of it (with the Envelope lab on, its Release is the one used), shortened to end by the hard limit or a pattern’s own end; a note that reaches either, or a Trigger note’s end, fades over the release it started with.

    Browser: · Platform: · Audio:

    MIDI input

    Level calibration

    Put a known external acoustic reference on the microphone (typically a calibrator that produces 94 dB re 20 µPa at 1 kHz), switch it on and capture it here. OSCILLA reads its level through the same input as a measurement; the offset is the reference minus the reading. It is valid only for this microphone, input gain, browser settings and position: OSCILLA records the input (as far as the browser reports it) and stops applying the calibration when the input changes. It is kept in page memory only: a reload or a closed tab discards it, and the browser asks first while one is set.

    Capturing opens the microphone for s. The recording is discarded as soon as its level is read: only the level reading and the facts of the input are kept.
